guard.failures_escalate: {count} consecutive failures, at least twice the limit of {limit}; escalate.
guard.same_error: The last two failed attempts share error signature {signature}.
guard.no_progress: {count} commands ran with no change in the progress fingerprint (window {window}).
guard.verification: Verification {signature} failed {count} times with unchanged state (limit {limit}).
guard.timeout: The task has run for {elapsed}s, over the {limit}s limit. To continue, the human operator reviews it and runs 'wev guard acknowledge --run <run> --task <task> --reason <why>' in their own terminal; to allow longer tasks, raise limits.task_timeout_seconds for the next run.
guard.timeout_polling: The task is past its {limit}s limit but is waiting on a long-running process.
guard.help: Evaluate the execution guard over a recorded event history.
guard.evaluate.help: Judge an event history and print the guard verdict.
guard.evaluate.events: JSON file with a list of guard events (or an object with an 'events' list).
guard.evaluate.now: Current time in seconds; defaults to the latest event time.
guard.signature.help: Print the stable signature of a command.
guard.signature.cwd: Working directory that is part of the signature.
guard.signature.argv: Command and arguments, after a literal --.
guard.error.events_shape: The events file must hold a list of events or an object with an 'events' list.
guard.acknowledge.help: Human operator only: acknowledge a tripped guard verdict (STOP or ASK_HUMAN) so the guard counts again from now. Needs a terminal on stdin and stdout and a typed confirmation word; the audit log records the operating-system user, the terminal and the time. A determined process can fake a terminal, so with the Claude Code plugin this command also goes through Claude Code's permission prompt.
guard.acknowledge.task: Acknowledge only the events of this task. Without it the whole run is acknowledged.
guard.acknowledge.reason: Why it is safe to continue (recorded in the decision and the audit log).
guard.error.human_required: Refused: acknowledging a guard verdict is for the human operator, and this call did not come from a terminal. If you are an agent, stop and ask the human operator to review the verdict (wev guard check --run {run}) and to run 'wev guard acknowledge --run {run} --reason <why>' themselves in their own terminal.
guard.error.reason_required: A reason is required to acknowledge a guard verdict.
guard.error.not_tripped: Nothing to acknowledge: the guard is not tripped for this scope.
guard.acknowledge.run: Id of the run whose guard is acknowledged (required, so the choice is deliberate).
guard.cycle: The commands {signatures} keep repeating in the same order with no progress in between (more than {limit} rounds).
guard.polling_cap: {count} polling commands in a row (cap {limit}); a person must decide whether to keep waiting.
guard.confirm.acknowledge: You are about to ACKNOWLEDGE a guard verdict, so the guard counts again from now.
